description: Keeps host status UI, such as a connection banner, an error bar or a session-expiry strip, above every Tempo top-layer surface (TmModal, TmDialog, a modal TmDrawer, sheets, TmOverlayPanel popovers, the command palette). That includes surfaces opened after the content appeared. It is the declarative wrapper over TopLayerPinService, and it shares one pinned-on-top registry with the toast containers (decision TOP-LAYER-PIN, docs/top-layer-pin.md). Visibility is the signal: Visible=false renders the hidden attribute and the pin module hands the element back as a plain, hidden element, with no interop call per toggle. While a native modal <dialog> is open nothing is promoted above it, and the pin lands when the dialog closes. The root is exempt from a Tempo modal trap's inert background, so render it at layout level, outside the @Body wrapper. Position it through Class. The tm-pin-on-top class resets the browser popover defaults at zero specificity, so a fixed bottom bar stays a bar.

parameters.name: ChildContent
parameters.description: The pinned content: a status banner, a connection strip or an error bar.

parameters.name: Visible
parameters.description: Whether the content is shown. false renders the root with the hidden attribute, and the pin module demotes it.

parameters.name: Priority
parameters.description: Order between pinned elements. A higher value paints higher, and equal values keep render order. 0 is the band of the toast containers. Use 100 to paint above toasts.

parameters.name: Class
parameters.description: Additional CSS classes for the root. Position the element here (for example a fixed bottom bar).

examples.title: Connection banner above every modal
examples.code: <TmPinnedOnTop Visible="@_offline" Priority="100" Class="my-offline-bar" role="status">You are offline. Changes are saved locally.</TmPinnedOnTop>
